claims.text: On American Alchemy with Jesse Michels, 12 July 2025, at 0:58:13, Salas said he did not learn his own incident was at Oscar Flight rather than Echo Flight until 1996, when he reached his former commander Fred Meiwald, who told him 'we were not at Echo Flight. We were at Oscar flight'. Salas says he had spoken of the Echo Flight incident as his own because it was so similar to what he recalled. This is his own account of the discrepancy the board's node already records.

claims.text: On American Alchemy with Jesse Michels, 12 July 2025, at 0:28:33, Robert Salas said one of the documents received from the Air Force is a telex about the Echo Flight shutdown which names by name two individuals working for Boeing, in which SAC headquarters demanded a complete investigation and used the words 'this is of grave concern'. claims.text: At 0:39:39 Salas said he and James Klotz checked with the Department of Energy, cognizant of nuclear testing in Nevada, and that 'There were no nuclear tests on March 16th or March 24th', which on his account removes the nuclear-EMP explanation on the government's own records. He names no document number for the check.

claims.sourceText: American Alchemy with Jesse Michels, 'Air Force Officer: A UFO Shut Down 10 Nukes in Seconds (ft. Bob Salas)', 12 July 2025, 0:44:54 to 0:47:25
claims.text: At 0:44:54 to 0:47:25 Salas described the Boeing bench-test result: an injected electrical signal of a given frequency, voltage and duration could make one guidance and control system shut down, but the testers 'had no idea on how that could be injected into this each missile separately within seconds'; the cable run was about eight to nine inches in diameter and 'triply shielded against EMI'; the report concluded an external signal caused the shutdowns while stating they could not explain how it got in; and Salas says he and James Klotz later reached the two named testers, who repeated that they could not explain it.

claims.text: On American Alchemy with Jesse Michels, 12 July 2025, at 0:32:01, Robert Salas said that Ray Fowler was a manager under Sylvania Corporation, which held the contract for the electrical systems at Malmstrom, that Fowler's own contractor staff reported seeing the objects and being involved in the missile shutdowns, and that Fowler passed this to Roy Craig, the Colorado project's chief investigator, with names, dates, places and telephone numbers. Salas presents this as the reason Craig travelled to Malmstrom, and says at 0:32:49 that he holds the Chase interview on audio tape.
